title: example 287 preservation (Phase 5 step 1): BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches on vulnerable-release and fixed-release, native strict, expected established
description: The job runs python3 examples/tools/build.py 287 --task preservation, the target route of llm-dlc/loops/example-targets.md (Phase 5 step 1: each deep packet's claim tasks attempted once through the merged path). Example 287 is CVE-2025-22228 (Spring Security 6.3.7 -> 6.3.8, BCrypt ignored password bytes past 72), prepared by the published-artifact route (pinned Central JARs). Workflow plans the task from target.json; runtime prepares vulnerable-release and fixed-release, runs the packet's controls in separate JVMs on JDK 21 and 25, then runs jvmcontract prove (built by the runner from lib/ at this commit) with --engine native --gaps strict on org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder#matches(Ljava/lang/CharSequence;Ljava/lang/String;)Z with claims/in-range-matching-preserved.json (claim key 59e6744bcaca7b2b, preservation, bounds unwind 16, maxArrayLength 80). The claim: Outside the allowed change (a non-null candidate whose UTF-8 encoding is longer than 72 bytes), BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches ends alike on both releases, by result and exception class, for any candidate and stored value, null and malformed ones included: a valid in-range candidate still matches its stored hash, a wrong in-range candidate is still refused, and what the encoder does with a missing or malformed stored value is unchanged. A constant rejection satisfies the security property and fails this. Workflow ingests every record into one format-2 receipt under receipts/preservation/, and build.py exits 0 only when the receipt's matchesExpected is true. Predicted stops: the BCryptPasswordEncoder receiver, String.getBytes(UTF_8), BCrypt's stored-hash regex and its key schedule loops under unwind 16. A capability refusal is a successful diagnostic, not a pass: it gives an unresolved receipt, prints NOT AS EXPECTED and exits 1, and is read as an observed gap for the v1 gap inventory, with the claim left unresolved and never weakened. No proof of this task has been attempted before.
expected: example 287 task preservation gives its expected conclusion, established: build.py prints 'as expected' and exits 0. An observed capability refusal (unresolved, NOT AS EXPECTED, exit 1) is a recorded gap, not a pass

resources.notes: one pinned acquisition from Central (cached by sha256 after the first job), two short JVM control runs on JDK 21 and 25, one native strict jvmcontract proof, plus its cargo build if lib/'s tree isn't cached; the replay jobs of the same packet took a few minutes at under 1 GiB
